CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up for chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction and pre-operative clearance for right knee replacement surgery.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Nicole Miller is a patient with chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction who presents for follow-up. She had an exacerbation of congestive heart failure earlier in the spring with increasing dyspnea. BMP was 3,000 in March and increased to 6,000 in April, prompting medication adjustments. Her furosemide was changed to torsemide 20 milligrams by mouth daily, and her lisinopril was increased to 10 milligrams daily in March. She reports weight loss of approximately 3 to 3.5 pounds since last visit in April. She notes that the torsemide is helping and her urinary urgency is much better. She had bilateral leg cramps a few days ago that she attributes to being cold while sleeping; the cramps resolved after drinking pickle juice. She reports using the bathroom adequately. She has had no recent dyspnea and her breathing is non-labored. Patient is scheduled for right knee replacement surgery on June 24th and is interested in proceeding with this planned surgery. She also reports a history of heartburn that was briefly treated with prilosec in January for approximately two weeks but has since resolved. Patient is due for colonoscopy screening.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Negative for dyspnea, chest pain, or palpitations. Denies current heartburn. Denies active leg or finger cramps at present. Urinary function reported as good. Patient reports adequate kidney function and bathroom use.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction. History of anemia. Diabetes. Scheduled for right knee replacement surgery on June 24th. Overdue for colonoscopy screening.

MEDICATIONS
Torsemide 20 milligrams by mouth daily. Lisinopril 10 milligrams daily. Iron supplement. Clopidogrel. Prilosec (discontinued in January).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
No family history of colon cancer noted.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient appears well. Cardiovascular: Blood pressure is good. Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally; patient instructed to take deep breaths. Lungs sound pretty good. Non-labored breathing noted.

RESULTS
Hemoglobin level: Stable, doing well. Potassium: 3.9 (holding steady on torsemide). Creatinine: 0.7 (normal kidney function). BUN: 23 (slightly elevated, may indicate dehydration but not concerning). Magnesium: 1.7 (normal). Blood glucose: 169 today (non-fasting). Last A1C: 5.5 in March. Blood pressure: Good. BNP results pending from recent order (was 3,000 in March and 6,000 in April prior to medication adjustment). Recent chest X-ray available (no new imaging needed).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Chronic congestive heart failure with mixed presentation: Had exacerbation in spring. Switched from furosemide to torsemide; patient is doing much better symptomatically. Weight loss of 3 to 3.5 pounds. Non-labored breathing. Will repeat EKG today. Continue current regimen. Labs checked and creatinine is appropriate. Recommend magnesium supplementation twice daily to maintain levels around 2 range to help stabilize heart muscle. Patient will need to discontinue clopidogrel one week prior to surgery.

2. Pre-operative examination: Patient scheduled for right knee replacement surgery on June 24th at East Metro. Will complete pre-operative check within two weeks of surgery, during first or second week of June. May need to repeat EKG prior to surgery. No chest X-ray needed. No additional blood work needed at this time. Patient instructed to receive reminder regarding clopidogrel discontinuation one week prior to surgery.

3. Colonoscopy screening: Patient overdue for screening colonoscopy. Will attempt to schedule at Bartley Regional Hospital within next 30 days prior to insurance change. No family history of colon cancer. Procedure should not delay knee surgery. Options include Dr. Martin at County Surgical Services or Valley Medical at Springfield.

4. Diabetes: A1C was 5.1 on last check; no need for A1C today. May need repeat A1C prior to surgery next month.
